absent: Numeric values and semantics of SEMMSL SEMMNS SEMOPM SEMMNI SHMMAX SHMALL SHMMNI and CLONE_NEWIPC beyond their use as defaults and flags.
Behaviour of quota helpers, common namespace setup, tree identity and insertion, and user reference handling during creation.
Behaviour of message queue and control table setup, retirement and mount handling, including full msg_init_ns and msg_exit_ns implementations.
Identifier table, key hash, free_ipcs, freeary and do_shm_rmid semantics for semaphore and shared memory teardown.
Task lock, proxy, reference counting, capability check and conversion helpers for namespace get, put and ownership.
Workqueue pool, queue and worker struct layouts, colour meanings, barrier function, completion mechanisms and lockdep map handling.
Semaphore permission checks, operation evaluation, sleeper wakeup, status codes, undo application and security hooks.
Proc interface registration details and the exact layout of the semaphore status view beyond its header line.
RCU, list, mount, llist and memory allocation helper contracts used during reclamation and barrier handling.

findings.text: Provides a namespace duplication helper that retains the current set when the new IPC flag is absent and otherwise creates a fresh set bound to the given user namespace.
Offers a sleepable wait that blocks until the named work item has completed whether queued or already running, reporting whether a wait was needed.
Exposes initialization and teardown helpers for System V semaphore and shared memory state inside an IPC namespace, covering default limits, usage counters and identifier table setup and release.
Exposes a helper releasing debug tracking for stack allocated work and an accessor returning the private payload stored for a kernel thread.
Boot time setup for semaphore state that seeds defaults in the initial namespace and registers a readable status view for semaphore identifiers.
Deferred cleanup entry scheduled as work that reclaims a batch of retired IPC namespaces after isolating their message queue mounts and waiting out readers.

Single semaphore record holding a numeric value, a reference to the last modifier, dedicated spin protection, separate pending lists for altering and non altering single operations, plus a candidate timestamp for last operation.

Semaphore set header combining permission metadata and creation time, array wide pending lists for altering and non altering complex waits, undo linkage, member count, complex waiter count, a selector for global locking, and a trailing member vector.

Pending operation waiter linking into a queue, identifying the sleeper and requester, referencing undo state, carrying completion status, an operation vector with count and blocking pointer, plus flags for alteration and duplicate targets.
Per process undo record with process wide linkage and deferred release support, owner list back pointer, per set linkage, set identifier, and trailing per member adjustment values.
Per process container for undo records holding a reference count, spin protection and a head linking all records of that process.

Flush resolution runs under read side protection to map work to a pool, then takes the pool lock with interrupts masked to distinguish queued versus executing placement and to validate pool association before inserting a barrier.

Barrier insertion expects the pool lock held, assigns an inactive marker and a colour inherited from the target or executing worker, accounts in flight work, links after the target or worker position, and takes a pool reference.

Semaphore sets use two granularities: single member operations attempt a member spin lock when global mode appears clear and recheck with acquire ordering, while multi member operations hold the object lock and force global mode; release restores simple placement and decays the mode selector.
Namespace lookup for another task holds the task lock while sampling the proxy pointer and acquiring a reference, returning the generic portion or null when absent.

Namespace creation first obtains user quota, retrying once after waiting for pending asynchronous frees if quota is exhausted, then allocates zeroed storage, performs common setup and identity assignment, wires message queue, control tables and message, semaphore and memory subsystems in order, and on any failure unwinds already acquired resources in reverse before reporting an encoded error.

Semaphore initialization loads four control limits, clears usage and prepares the semaphore identifier partition; shared memory initialization loads three size and count limits, clears forced removal and total accounting and prepares its identifier partition.

Namespace destruction releases the message queue mount, exits semaphore, message and memory subsystems, retires both control tables, then drops quota and user references before common release and storage free.

Batch reclamation first detaches all collected mounts for short term handling, then waits for a read side grace period before destroying each namespace individually, isolating teardown from lingering readers.
Duplication shares the old set by reference when the creation flag is clear; otherwise it delegates to fresh creation with the supplied user and old namespaces as parameters.

Installation of a new IPC namespace requires administrative capability in both the target user namespace and the caller credential user namespace, and on success swaps the proxy pointer with proper reference handling; ownership query returns the stored user namespace.
When System V support is disabled the per namespace message, semaphore and memory setup and teardown helpers become empty operations that report success without touching state.

Pool mapping inspects work metadata atomically, returning an embedded queue pool when present, otherwise decoding an offline pool identifier and returning null for the none value or a table lookup result.
Colour handling packs a small integer into dedicated flag bits by shifting and extracts it by shifting and masking, preserving round trip conversion.

Current worker detection returns associated worker state only when running in task context with the worker flag set, via thread private data; conversion to thread control state warns when the caller lacks the kernel thread flag.
Work activation tracking and bottom half callback waiting have dual builds where one performs real bookkeeping or lock acquisition and the other is an empty operation, selected by configuration.

Flush proceeds from lookup to conditional barrier enqueue with completion tracking, then waits for completion and destroys stack state; absence of pool association yields no wait, while cancel origin on bottom half work uses a spinning wait.

Global mode selection uses a countdown initialized to a hysteresis constant on entry, refreshed while already global, and decayed on each global release until reaching zero with release ordering, but never leaving while complex waiters remain.

Entering complex handling splices every member altering queue into the set wide altering queue; leaving with no complex waiters moves each set wide waiter back to the queue of its first target member and reinitializes the set wide head; final set memory is released via a callback that also drops security state.
Flushing a non reclaim capable queue from reclaim context is diagnosed, covering direct reclaim flagged tasks and reclaim workers, while cancel origin and reclaim capable targets are exempt.
Flushing from inside single threaded or rescuer equipped queues is forced to trip lock dependency tracking to reveal deadlock when the flush cannot make progress.
Flush start warns and reports no work when the subsystem is offline, when the operation pointer is missing, or when the item is neither queued nor executing, avoiding a wait on untracked state.

Cancel path waiting for bottom half execution spins on completion rather than sleeping, with an extra callback drain step on realtime builds to avoid live lock when preempting soft interrupt handling.
Fast path stack sizing constants provide 256 for maximum members per set and 64 for maximum operations per call.
Hysteresis constant for remaining in global lock mode is 10.
Sentinel negative one denotes that the global object lock rather than a member index is held.
Four control aliases map positionally to slots zero through three of the semaphore control table.
Accessor selects the semaphore partition from the namespace identifier array.
